subject: Sizing ask for APAC pilot & regional commitments
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acuityhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask for APAC pilot & regional commitments

Marcus / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acuity is ready to move to a pilot focused in APAC, with a 3-month evaluation and the potential to expand EU and US pools if the pilot meets latency and cost targets. A few specifics from our side to help you size:

- Target geographies: Singapore (primary), Sydney (secondary), EU (Germany) for alpha.
- Initial traffic estimate: ~1.5M inference tokens/day in APAC during pilot (~45M tokens/month).
- Latency SLO: median end-to-end <150ms for short chat prompts (avg seq length ~120 tokens).
- Model: expect to run a 13B LLaMA-family model variant.
- Preferred HW: would like a small H100 pool for latency-critical endpoints and A100/Q8 for lower-cost batch workloads.
- Procurement timeline: we'd like pricing and a firm pool availability commit by end of June to include in our procurement packet.

Can you provide a concrete recommended commit (GPU count by region + warm standby), expected lead times to provision, and a ballpark committed monthly spend? Also please attach any template MOU or draft SLA.

Chris
Chris Nolan
Head of AI Product, Acuity Health
chris.nolan@acuityhealth.com

Attachment: acuity-rfp-summary.pdf (1 page)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for APAC pilot & regional commitments

Chris — thanks, this is clear and helpful. I've looped Karthik and Lauren to get a quick sizing + commercial sketch.

High-level approach we recommend:
1) APAC pilot: a small H100 latency pool (hot) + A100 spot-style pool (warm) for cost.
2) EU alpha: A100-only pool sized for expected overflow/peaks during business hours.
3) US: keep a minimal warm pool for failover / burst.

I'll attach an initial proposal (APAC-focused) and a sizing workbook with assumptions so you can tweak usage. Two quick asks for accuracy: a) confirm peak concurrent requests expected (or p95 qps) during pilot, and b) expected retention of KV cache between sessions (session affinity).

Proposed next steps: internal sizing by EOD Friday, then a short call early next week to align on commit levels and draft MOU.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Dedicated Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: apac-proposal-v1.pdf, apac-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for APAC pilot & regional commitments

On Fri, May 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM Marcus Lin wrote:
> Chris — thanks, this is clear and helpful. I've looped Karthik and Lauren to get a quick sizing + commercial sketch.

Quick technical sizing notes from my side (assumptions: 13B model, 120 token avg, batch target 4-8, KV cache enabled with 30% hit rate):

- Target inference throughput (APAC pilot): ~2.5 qps sustained per endpoint (p95 spikes to 20 qps).
- Latency profile: H100 gives ~40-60ms token latency for this model at our optimized runtime; A100/Q8 ~80-120ms.

Suggested committed pools (conservative, includes room for canary + warm standby):
- APAC (SG/SYD combined): 6x H100 (hot) + 4x A100 (warm/batch).
- EU (DE): 4x A100 (hot with autoscale to 6x for peak periods).
- US (VA-region): 2x A100 (warm standby, fast failover routing).

Rationale: 6 H100s should cover median load with 20% headroom; A100 warm nodes handle batch scenarios and reduce per-token cost. Warm standby means we keep images and KV cache primed; cold provisioning lead time for GPUs is ~2-4 weeks for cloud reservations, 6-8 weeks for dedicated baremetal procurement.

Estimated committed monthly token capacity and ballpark spend (very rough):
- APAC committed: 45M tokens/month -> expected committed spend range $45k-$65k/mo depending on exact GPU mix and batching efficiency.
- EU committed: 25M tokens/month -> $20k-$30k/mo.
- US standby: nominal committed buffer $6k-$10k/mo.

I'll prepare a short scenarios table (low/medium/high) and include quantized cost per 1M tokens for each mix.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acuityhealth.com>, Acuity Health Procurement <procurement@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for APAC pilot & regional commitments

Chris — following up with a concrete, commit-based option for your procurement packet. Attached is a short MOU draft and the sizing spreadsheet with three scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive). Summary below: 

Option B (recommended baseline for pilot + enterprise readiness):
- APAC: 6x H100 (hot), 4x A100 (warm). Warm standby kept primed with KV cache.
- EU: 4x A100 (hot) with autoscale to 6x (burst).
- US: 2x A100 (warm standby).
- SLA: 99.9% regional availability for hot pools; latency SLOs tied to model variant and sequence lengths.
- Pricing (committed monthly): APAC $55,000/mo, EU $24,000/mo, US buffer $8,000/mo. One-time setup fee: $12,000 (networking, secure VPC onboarding).
- Lead times: hot pool provisioning (cloud-reserved) 7-14 business days after PO; baremetal/private 6-8 weeks.

We can add a 20% burst credit for sales-driven spikes in month 1 at no extra cost to help you validate peak behavior.

Next actions: 1) confirm Option B and procurement contact, 2) we schedule a 30-min technical handoff to align curves and cache behavior, 3) finalize MOU and PO.

If helpful I can open a HubSpot deal record and upload the MOU so procurement can link it to your packet.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Dedicated Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: mou-draft-acuity.docx

Marcus — this looks good and more concrete than we expected, thanks. Procurement looped in and they asked for the following before they can issue a PO: 1) final MOU with billing cadence and termination terms, 2) a named technical contact for onboarding, and 3) confirmation of data residency controls for SG/DE.

Can we set a 30-minute call on Tuesday to go over the tech handoff and confirm the MOU language? Also, please send a one-pager that summarizes the Option B numbers for exec review.

Ill introduce our procurement lead on the call.

Best,
Chris Nolan
Head of AI Product, Acuity Health
